reviews.title: No longer usable
reviews.text:
I have been using OneNote since 2018 on my iPad 6th generation. I have kept updating to latest version. 

Today OneNote cannot be opened anymore. The app just flash quits itself. Unfortunately the newer version of OneNote requires iOS 18, but my iPad can only be updated to iPadOS17. My current OneNote version is 16.23. Every update is irreversibly cornering me into this dead end.

There are other serious bugs on the non-updatable version. The sync stopped working for quite a while, so all my work have been on local caches. After noticing glitches, I tried backups and upgrades. For backups, it turned out rather impossible. Export to pdf can only done per page, and I had more than 100 pages, and each export is not responsive (perhaps part of the glitches). iPad-to-Mac backups don’t seem to back up the unsynced caches (checked by running some database tests).

There are deep and fundamental issues with the software engineering behind this app. Please allow backward compatibility. I hope I can access my notes. I know my iPad is old, but none of the other apps have such an issue.

reviews.title: Plagued with issues every update; excluded older OS versions from vital bug fix
reviews.text:
I’m a college student. I’ve been using OneNote since high school to take notes. I’ve had the same iPad since then. It worked for the most part—but I’ve had to deal with obnoxious bugs throughout my years using the app. (auto-deselecting a marker when I use my Apple Pencil to write, extremely clunky syncing making it difficult to access my notes, version differences appearing for no reason, etc.) They’ve never made the app literally unusable until now. 

In the past month, I discovered that the app wasn’t syncing with my laptop version of OneNote. I tried to sign in with my University Microsoft account, and it didn’t work. I just got stuck. I tried uninstalling but that didn’t fix it- instead it just locked me out of taking notes on my iPad at all. I tried installing PowerPoint as a workaround but I had to install an older version due to my iPad’s age and it has this problem too. I looked into it online and other people have been having this problem, but most people say it’s been fixed with the newest update. 

Here’s the problem: you pushed the recent update that caused the issue, but then you limited the update that actually *fixes* the issue to IOS 18 and above. Three months ago I could take notes just fine. Now my iPad is apparently obsolete. I don’t know if you can push updates that are compatible with older versions, but if you can, please fix this. I literally cannot use the app without it and this planned obsolescence outcome is absolutely infuriating.

reviews.title: DO NOT USE THE MOVE FEATURE
reviews.text: Hello, I use this app for most of my particular writing needs, although the 365 desktop version is infinitely better. It’s great, easy to use and quick and simple. BUT. This app likes to crash occasionally, and has no undo feature which can result in a lot lost work if you’re not careful…but, never, and I say never, ever use the “move” feature. If you move a large enough section of sections with a group tab, everything may be forever lost. For some bloody reason, all your moved data is still local on your phone, but all that data becomes unable to sync. EVER. Even copying parts of that moved data will cause the app to infinitely load for nothing. This results in an utterly painful nightmare where you have to manually copy the text of everything to a new notebook or set of sections and tabs. Until Microsoft bothers to fix this problem, I will never, ever recommend using this app. Speaking all my stuff is already on OneNote, I’m obligated to the sunk cost fallacy. If it wasn’t these two rather egregious issues, I would recommend the app. Otherwise, no. Just no
